title: De motu vibratorio laminarum elasticarum, ubi plures novae vibrationum species hactenus non pertractatae evolvuntur

deep.reconstruction:
The page belongs to Euler's systematic treatment of the transverse vibrations of an elastic lamina (Euler–Bernoulli beam) under different end conditions. The modal shape is y = A cos Φ + B sin Φ + C e^Φ + D e^{−Φ}, with Φ = θx/b and time factor cos θθt. At the right end Φ = ζ = θa/b.

(1) Corollary to Problem III (both ends pinned, 'stylo defixa'). On the previous page the conditions y = 0 and y'' = 0 at each end gave A = 0, D = −C, then C = 0 and sin ζ = 0, so ζ = iπ. The frequencies therefore go as i² (π, 4π, 9π, 16π times b²/a²). Euler remarks that these tones are 'regular and harmonic among themselves', i.e. the frequency ratios are rational (the squares). He also says they are somewhat graver (lower) than those of Problem III's predecessor, the pinned–free lamina. That is right: π² ≈ 9.87 is less than 3.9266² ≈ 15.42.

(2) Problem IV: end A pinned, end B clamped ('muro infixa').
- At A the conditions are the same as before, so A = 0 and D = −C. The reaction carried by the pin is E = −Kc²(θ³/b³) cos θθt (−B + C − D), which is proportional to y'''(0).
- At B the conditions are y(a) = 0 and y'(a) = 0. With A = 0 and D = −C these become
  B sin ζ + C(e^ζ − e^{−ζ}) = 0,
  B cos ζ + C(e^ζ + e^{−ζ}) = 0.
- On the next page these combine to tan ζ = tanh ζ. This is the same characteristic equation as the pinned–free lamina, so the spectrum is the same (ζ ≈ 3.9266, 7.0686, …).

In modern terms this is the clamped–pinned beam, whose eigenvalues coincide with the nonzero eigenvalues of the pinned–free beam. Euler states this explicitly in the corollary on the following page and starts to interpret it as a correspondence between a free end and a clamped end.
errors: No mathematical errors on this page. The boundary equations and the reduction with A=0, D=−C are correct.

Minor: the 'graver' comparison in the Corollary tacitly ignores the zero-frequency rigid-rotation mode of the pinned–free lamina. Its first elastic mode (ζ≈3.927) is indeed higher than the pinned–pinned fundamental (ζ=π).

ideas.what: Pinned–pinned beam has frequencies proportional to i² (harmonic in the sense of rational ratios), lower than the pinned–free beam
ideas.modern_name: Simply supported Euler–Bernoulli beam eigenfrequencies ω_n ∝ n²π²
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (E443, 1773), building on D. Bernoulli and Euler's 1740s beam work
ideas.where_published: E443, Novi Commentarii Acad. Petrop. 17; discussed by Truesdell in Opera omnia II.11(2)

ideas.what: Clamped condition y=0, y'=0 at one end combined with a pinned end, giving the characteristic equation tan ζ = tanh ζ
Shear reaction at the pin is proportional to y'''(0)
ideas.modern_name: Support reaction / shear force at a simple support

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard textbook boundary-value results. The coincidence of the clamped–pinned and pinned–free spectra is known (Rayleigh's Theory of Sound) and Euler's own observation of it is recorded in Truesdell's commentary on E443. Nothing here appears absent from the literature.
transcription_corrections: The transcription matches the image; 'ſtilo' (sic) in the Corollary is Euler's own spelling.
'Ae=E' is correct as printed, denoting the force Aε at the pin A.
